text: Good API design makes software easier to use and maintain. For REST APIs, choose clear endpoints that match resources, such as /users or /orders. Use the correct HTTP methods (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE) and return meaningful status codes, like 200 for success or 404 when something is missing. Always write clear documentation so other developers understand how to call your endpoints. Versioning is also important: when you change your API, keep older versions working so existing apps do not break. Finally, keep responses simple and consistent. These practices help teams build reliable systems that are easy to integrate and support over time.
